subjects.name: none
subjects.config: No gateway or checker: the calls go straight to the FHIR server and the agent's report is the only account of what was stored.

subjects.name: http-status
subjects.config: Trusts the status code: a 2xx answer means the call did what it asked (a Bundle, every entry), anything else did nothing. It reads nothing back and raises no flag.

subjects.name: deedglass
subjects.config: deedglass serve built from this commit. Every agent call goes through the Gate as its own action, to a fhir connector with default settings (if_match when_known), each write read back at the version the server reported (Checked, L1) and Proven (L2) from Medplum's change log, with meta.author checked against the agent's client. The policy is the healthcare-fhir pack's refusals with writes allowed at L1 (bench/cmd/fhir-bench/policy.yaml). A Bundle or a conditional update goes through a REST connector (the fhir connector takes one resource per call), which records the call (L0, Claimed).

scenarios.title: A conditional create answers 200 and stores nothing
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 conditional create: with one match, the server ignores the create and answers 200 OK with the existing resource. Medplum does exactly that.

scenarios.title: A conditional update with no match creates a second Patient
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 conditional update: with no match and no id in the body, the server creates the resource. Medplum documents the same: if no matching resource is found, one is created from the given data.

scenarios.title: A transaction Bundle is applied in part
scenarios.behaviour: Medplum documents that without the transaction-bundles feature flag a transaction Bundle is processed as a batch, with no atomicity and no error or warning. FHIR R4 batch entries are processed independently.

scenarios.title: The same transaction with the feature on is refused whole
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 transaction: the server accepts every entry or rejects them all. Medplum applies transactions atomically when the project's transaction-bundles feature flag is on.

scenarios.title: An AccessPolicy's read-only field is dropped from a 201
scenarios.stored_without_a_gateway: create 1 Observation; Observation.note not as the agent believes
scenarios.behaviour: Medplum AccessPolicy read-only elements: the client can't set the element. On Medplum 5.2.6 a create that sets one is answered 201 and stored without it (the behaviour examples/medplum shows).

scenarios.title: The id the agent chose is replaced by the server's
scenarios.stored_without_a_gateway: create 1 Observation; Observation.id not as the agent believes
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 create: if the resource has an id, the server SHALL ignore it and assign its own.

scenarios.title: The author the agent set is replaced by its client
scenarios.stored_without_a_gateway: create 1 Observation; Observation.meta.author not as the agent believes
scenarios.behaviour: Medplum keeps meta.author as a server-managed element: it records the client that wrote the resource, and names a user the client acts for in meta.onBehalfOf (the X-Medplum-On-Behalf-Of header).

scenarios.title: The server adds meta, and nothing else changes
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4: the server maintains meta.versionId and meta.lastUpdated on every write; Medplum also records meta.author and meta.project.

scenarios.title: An update without If-Match overwrites another writer's change
scenarios.stored_without_a_gateway: update 1 Observation; overwrote 1 Observation version the agent hadn't read
scenarios.behaviour: Without version checking the last write wins (FHIR R4 managing contention; Medplum's updating-data guide). If-Match would make the server answer 412 instead (scenario 10).

scenarios.title: The same update with If-Match is refused with 412
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 and Medplum: with If-Match naming a version that is no longer current, the update fails with 412 Precondition Failed.

scenarios.title: A JSON Patch add replaces the identifiers instead of appending
scenarios.stored_without_a_gateway: update 1 Observation; Observation.identifier not as the agent believes
scenarios.behaviour: RFC 6902 add: if the target member exists, its value is replaced (appending to an array is /identifier/-). Medplum documents that add replaces any value at the path.

scenarios.title: A JSON Patch on a missing element is refused
scenarios.behaviour: RFC 6902 replace: the target location MUST exist. Medplum answers 400.

scenarios.title: An Observation for a patient that doesn't exist is stored
scenarios.stored_without_a_gateway: create 1 Observation; 1 reference in Observation.subject to a resource that doesn't exist
scenarios.behaviour: Medplum's referential integrity on write is an optional project setting (Project.checkReferencesOnWrite), off unless a project turns it on.

scenarios.title: The same Observation is refused when references are checked
scenarios.behaviour: With Project.checkReferencesOnWrite on, Medplum refuses a create whose reference target doesn't exist.

scenarios.title: A deleted Observation stays readable in history
scenarios.stored_without_a_gateway: delete 1 Observation; 1 deleted Observation still readable in history
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 delete doesn't remove a resource's version history. Medplum's delete is a soft delete; $expunge removes a resource and its history.

scenarios.title: A retry after a lost answer stores the reading twice
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 create isn't idempotent: each create stores a new resource. Conditional create is the standard's way to avoid duplicates.

scenarios.title: Another system changes the order's status after the agent
scenarios.behaviour: FHIR R4 update: each update stores a new version; a later writer's version is that writer's, not the agent's.
